assessment.nobel_worthiness: Combines new data with an explanatory framework. The China-shock work measures how trade exposure changes local labour markets, and the task-based and polarization work explains how technology changes labour demand and wage inequality. It has reshaped research and policy debate on labour markets, trade and inequality, which fits the criterion of significant societal impact through the research itself and the work it inspired.
assessment.attribution: The China-shock contributions are most cleanly credited to Autor, Dorn and Hanson. Katz is credited on the wage-structure and skill-demand literature but is left off to stay within three names, and he is also on B002. The task-based framework has a wider intellectual lineage that this ballot entry only partly captures.
assessment.maturity: More than fifteen years of replication, extension and critique. The long-run persistence and magnitude of the local effects have been debated, but the core empirical finding and the research design have stood up and become standard.
uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers the labour-demand and task contribution or the trade-shock contribution, which affects the choice of three names.
Overlap with recent prizes on technology and labour-market history (Goldin 2023, and 2024 and 2025 work on institutions and technological growth).
Debate over the external validity and persistence of the China-shock estimates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population administrative data have made intergenerational mobility measurable at fine geographic scale. This has changed the empirical study of opportunity and neighbourhood effects, and quasi-experimental designs have identified causal place effects. The contribution is a large data-and-measurement advance with an explanatory design and clear influence on research and policy.
assessment.attribution: Chetty is the central figure, with Hendren and Friedman closely tied to the core mobility and neighbourhood-effects papers. Katz is a major co-author on the Moving to Opportunity reanalysis. Credit is heavily team-based and concentrated in one research group.
assessment.maturity: Core papers date from about 2014 to 2022. Replications and follow-ups are growing but the long-run record is shorter than for older candidates. The honour may be somewhat early, though impact is already very large.
uncertainties: Whether the field has enough distance from the original findings to judge durability.
Concentration of credit in a single group, and Chetty also appearing on B025.
Dependence on proprietary or restricted administrative data, which limits independent replication.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantile regression is a foundational method, used throughout applied economics, especially to study distributional effects beyond the mean in wages, inequality, education and crime. It is a durable general-purpose tool of the kind that has been recognised before in econometrics.
assessment.attribution: Bassett and Koenker introduced it in 1978, and Koenker developed the theory, computation and inference in later decades. Chernozhukov is credited to the subfield but his contribution is better placed on later extensions, and he appears on other ballot entries, so he is not proposed.
assessment.maturity: Nearly fifty years of use and wide adoption, so the confirmation is among the strongest on the list.
uncertainties: Possible competition within econometrics from other methods candidates.
Whether methods work is judged less urgent than substantive empirical advances.
Intellectual precursors in the earlier robust-statistics literature.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Bayesian persuasion and information design set up a tractable framework for how a sender can optimally shape what others know. It is used in applications ranging from regulation and disclosure to platforms and auctions. It is a genuinely new theoretical object that built a large literature and sits alongside mechanism design and information economics, which have already been recognised.
assessment.attribution: The Kamenica–Gentzkow 2011 paper is the origin. Bergemann and Morris extended the idea to a general information-design programme and a robust version. Four names are credited and only three can be chosen, so one of Bergemann and Morris is a harder call. Gentzkow's separate empirical media work could complicate how his name is framed.
assessment.maturity: About fifteen years of rapid growth. The framework is now widely taught, though empirical tests are fewer than the volume of theory.
uncertainties: Choice among Kamenica, Gentzkow, Bergemann and Morris.
Limited direct empirical confirmation relative to the theoretical output.
Possible overlap with earlier information-economics prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Tax-record data were assembled into long historical series on top incomes and wealth, and offshore wealth was measured. This created new facts that reoriented debate and research on inequality and taxation. It is a clear case of data discovery with a conceptual framing, and its influence on research and society is very large. Under common criteria, political salience is not a factor.
assessment.attribution: Piketty and Saez are the originators of the top-incomes series, Zucman extended the work to wealth and offshore holdings, and Atkinson, who is deceased, was a key early contributor. Attribution is clear but is complicated by the late co-founder and by the roles of the World Inequality Database collaborators.
assessment.maturity: Core series date from the early 2000s and the data are widely used. The theoretical explanation (for example the r>g argument) and some measurement choices have been contested, so confirmation is stronger for the empirical facts than for the explanatory claims.
uncertainties: Contested methodology and conclusions in parts of the wealth and capital-share work.
Whether the contribution is judged more as measurement than as explanatory theory.
The committee may weigh the deceased Atkinson's role.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Political-economy models of trade protection (the 'protection for sale' framework) and the open-economy models linking trade, innovation and growth are a coherent, theoretically deep body of work. They changed how economists treat trade policy as an endogenous outcome of interest-group politics and how trade interacts with growth.
assessment.attribution: Grossman and Helpman are a stable, decades-long partnership, so joint credit is natural. Helpman also appears on B041 (firm heterogeneity), which complicates a clean assignment of his contributions.
assessment.maturity: Foundational work from the 1990s with decades of use, so maturity is high. The empirical confirmation of the protection-for-sale model has been mixed.
uncertainties: Mixed empirical support for the specific protection-for-sale predictions.
Overlap of the trade-theory space with B041 and B042, and the earlier recognition of trade theory.
Whether the growth and trade contributions or the political-economy contribution would be emphasised.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Intertemporal open-economy macroeconomics gave the modern foundation for analysing current accounts, exchange rates and international financial integration. The exchange-rate disconnect and related puzzles organised decades of research, and the textbook framework shaped policy analysis.
assessment.attribution: Obstfeld and Rogoff co-developed the framework, including the 'new open economy macroeconomics' work. Rogoff also appears on B033 with Reinhart, which splits the identification of his main contribution across two ballot entries.
assessment.maturity: Mature, from the 1990s with decades of consolidation. Some of the puzzles remain unresolved, which is a point both for the framework's importance and against its completeness.
uncertainties: Whether the contribution is perceived as foundational and distinctive or as a synthesis of earlier ideas.
Competition within macroeconomics from other candidates.
Rogoff's work being credited across more than one ballot entry.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Heterogeneous-agent New Keynesian models embed household heterogeneity and the distribution of wealth and marginal propensities to consume into monetary and fiscal transmission. The framework has changed how macroeconomists model policy and connects empirical micro evidence to aggregate analysis. It is an important methodological and conceptual advance.
assessment.attribution: The Kaplan–Moll–Violante 2018 paper is the clear anchor and the three are tightly linked. Other contributors to heterogeneous-agent macro (for example the earlier Aiyagari–Bewley–Huggett tradition) are not on this entry and would complicate how much is credited to this framework alone.
assessment.maturity: The most recent of the strong candidates, with the main contribution from around 2018. The framework is already widely adopted at central banks and in research, but long-run confirmation and empirical discipline are still developing.
uncertainties: Whether the contribution is too recent for a prize.
Dependence on earlier heterogeneous-agent macro foundations, and how the committee would treat those.
Calibration sensitivity and open questions on how well the models fit micro and macro evidence together.
